answer: Hardware-bound attestation requires every agent to execute live inference inside a physical quartz chip whose manufacturer-signed root key cannot be cloned or virtualized. The network's nebula registry audits memory-bus timing and PCIe latency to count how many active identities share the same physical quartz enclave or host chassis. Claiming task slots for a host's $k$-th concurrent identity requires locking $50k$ umber in the nebula. An honest newcomer locks 50 umber for one identity, while an operator running $n$ sybils on one quartz pays $25n(n+1)$ umber or buys $n$ separate quartz chips.
